html:
The battle in 490 BCE in which the army of Athens, with help from the small town of Plataea, defeated a Persian force that had landed on the plain of Marathon, northeast of the city.

Darius I of the Achaemenid Empire sent the expedition to punish Athens and Eretria for helping the Ionian Revolt of the Greek cities of Asia Minor. His commanders, Datis and Artaphernes, burned Eretria and landed at Marathon. The Athenians marched out and faced them for several days. Then, on the advice of the general Miltiades, their heavy infantry, the hoplites, charged at a run. The Greek centre gave way but the wings won and closed in. According to Herodotus, 6,400 Persians died against 192 Athenians.

The rest of the Persian force sailed round to Athens but found the army back home and left. It was the first time Greeks had beaten a Persian army in the open, and the dead of Marathon became heroes. The playwright Aeschylus fought there and asked that only this be on his tomb. Ten years later Persia came back in greater force, under Xerxes.

The tale of a runner who ran from Marathon to Athens with the news and died is a later legend. It inspired the marathon race at the first modern Olympics in 1896.
sum: The battle in 490 BCE in which the army of Athens, with help from the small town of Plataea, defeated a Persian force that had landed on the plain of Marathon, northeast of the city.
